typography.usage: Record IDs, states and notebook labels.

recognitionRules: Use a dark green ground with pale green reading text and lime highlights.
Keep a stable side rail for filters and notebook context.
Use monospaced text for record IDs and evaluation states.
Give evidence and uncertainty their own fields within each log entry.

principles: Move from observation to interpretation to a bounded next question.
Use the identity’s sample as a rhythm and vocabulary reference, not as a factual project claim.
voice.sample: Record the attempt. Keep the result and the doubt together.
voice.sampleStatus: Original fictional brand copy authored for this guide, not a quotation or factual claim.
avoid: Avoid “proves” when the material only supports a hypothesis.
Avoid invented testimonials, performance claims and quotation attribution.
voice.secondaryExample: A record suggests a direction; it does not speak for every person.
voice.cadence: Short opening, concrete follow-through; vary sentence length for explanation.

logoDirection: Use TRIAL LEDGER in Menlo with a small open square followed by a record number. Do not use a checkmark as the default symbol.
invariants: Use a dark green ground with pale green reading text and lime highlights.
Keep a stable side rail for filters and notebook context.
Use monospaced text for record IDs and evaluation states.
adaptations: Print exports replace dark fills with ruled entries.
A compact view can hide detail only when the full record remains reachable.
Keep the full name with any new symbol until the audience can recognize it independently.

fonts.sourceFontDependency: Menlo is an Apple/system font; not bundled.
system-ui resolves to a host-dependent operating-system UI font; original family is not identifiable or bundled.

clearSpaceRule: One open-record-square width around the complete identifier and name.

minimumSize.status: Conservative production recommendation after inspection at primary220px, secondary180px and symbols32/64px. Trial Ledger record code and Orbit descriptor motivate larger full-lockup minima; use secondary in narrow spaces.
